summary: No proposals. Cash is $71.62 (11.5% of $621.53 equity), only about $9.5 above the 10% buffer, and the book is already about 88.5% invested, inside the owner's 80-90% target. A buy that small would be a token-sized add (L4), on a day when October CPI printed hot (+0.4% m/m) and December hike odds are 82-99%. I reviewed every held position against its invalidation using the 11-09 marks in inputs/market.json and the stored mark-to-market, and none has tripped. SPY 752.69 is 3.4% above the 727.98 200-day line that VOO and VTI invalidate on; IDXX is about 706 vs the $630 stop; BND is about 71.6 vs $70.0; IEF is about 91.5 vs 89.5; VNQ is about 97.3 vs its roughly 5% stop; DPZ is about 334 vs $285; CARG is about 34.5 vs about $28.25; VRSN is about 306 vs 278; MSM is about 118.4 vs about $108; MSCI is about 646 vs a stop 8% under the $605.15 fill; WMT is about 125.7 vs a stop 7% under entry; KR is about 68 vs a stop 8% under the $64.88 fill; FAST is above 10% under the $51.89 fill. Following L1 and L5, the stops that drift furthest from the mark after the run-up are IDXX (about 11% under the mark) and DPZ (about 15% under); re-anchoring them is the Portfolio Manager's job through thesis_updates, not a trade slot. Following L3, the Staples stack (WMT, DPZ, KR) is still about 26% of equity by label, and IDXX plus any INCY add would be one Health Care sleeve, so I am not adding to either. If cash rises, INCY is the first non-Technology, non-Staples candidate (Fundamentals rank 10, F-score 8/9), with its guidance flattered by the one-time $246M CMS benefit and an IDXX overlap to size for. Market Analyst is risk-on at 0.4 confidence, but with a hot CPI and QQQ near its 200-day line I see no case to deploy the buffer.
